newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Texas Utilities CEO details Enserch deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Texas Utilities CEO details Enserch deal.

text.p: Texas Utilities Co President and Chief Executive Erle Nye on Friday said the company's acquisition of Enserch Corp would dilute earnings in the first year but would bring "substantial" benefits beginning in the third year.

"We think it will be five to six cents dilutive in the first full year of operation. It will be at worst break-even in the second year, and we would expect to have substantial contributions to earnings in the third year and after. Not only earnings, but cash flow as well," Nye said in an interview.
He said combining Texas Utilities and Enserch Corp, the largest electric and gas companies in Texas, in a $1.7 billion merger would allow the expanded company to offer combined services to customers.
"I would say we will have at a minimum $800 to $850 million in savings over the next 10 years. I think that is highly probable, and we should be able to do even better," Nye said.
Texas Utilities shareholders earlier approved the acquisition, and Enserch shareholders were to vote on it on Friday afternoon.

Under the deal, Texas Utilities will acquire Enserch's distribution and pipeline companies, Lone Star Gas and Lone Star Pipeline, with about $550 million of Texas Utilities common stock and $1.15 billion in debt and preferred stock.
Before the transaction is carried out, Enserch will spin off its 83 percent-owned exploration and production company, Enserch Exploration Inc.
Texas Utilities' earnings have risen sharply this year, helped by unusually hot weather in Texas this summer, as well as by cost savings and firm revenue growth.
Nye said he was comfortable with analysts' consensus view of 1996 earnings at $3.30 to $3.35 a share. "I wouldn't argue with that," he said.

He said earnings growth would likely slow next year if weather conditions return to normal, but he was confident the company can post average earnings growth of more than 5 percent annually for the next several years.
"We are serving an area of the country where the growth of the economy and of customers is very positive," Nye said.
